subject: Day 44: bath-time narration
bodyText:
Today's focus
The nightly bath becomes a multisensory language lab this week. Slow narration of each step turns a routine task into concentrated language input, and a predictable wind-down anchors sleep-onset cues.

Action items
- Treat bath time as enrichment, narrating each step slowly: warm water, soap on his shoulders, lift the arm, splash. Continuous narration during awake-alert time is the right target for this age. AAP HealthyChildren: baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Name each body part and action as you go. Across 18-plus months of nightly baths, this adds up to enormous cumulative exposure, and conversational turns matter more than raw volume. PubMed: Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Confirm the 2-month visit is on the calendar within the day 56-70 window and keep the feeding and output log current to bring along. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Increased drool and brief eye-rolling at sleep transitions remain normal; the drool is salivary maturation, not early teething.
- [monitor] No social smile in response to your face or voice yet. Many infants smile by now; note it for the 2-month visit if absent by 8 weeks.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting beyond 24 hours, or refusal of several feeds in a row.
- [call now] A rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 3 months, blue color around the lips, or labored breathing. For blue lips or an unresponsive episode, call 911 now!

Enrichment opportunities
- Use the bath as a multisensory station: warm water, slow narration, and gentle skin contact give Avi coordinated touch, sound, and temperature input in one routine. AAP HealthyChildren: baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Read a short board book during the wind-down after the bath to pair settling with shared reading and start an early sleep-onset cue. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Pause after each narrated step and respond to any coo or movement Avi offers, keeping the serve-and-return cadence alive even before words. PubMed: Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 56-70 (Jul 6-20): 2-month well visit; vaccines due are HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, and IPV #1.
- Day 57-72 (Jul 7-22): the 24-48h post-vaccine window, when low-grade fever, drowsiness, and fussiness are expected.
- Day 84-91 (early August): the sleep consolidation window opens near 3 months, a good point to lock in a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126 (Aug 31-Sep 14): 4-month well visit with the second vaccine round.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
